newsitem.title: UK: Key world closing stock market indices, July 4.
newsitem.headline: Key world closing stock market indices, July 4.

text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Friday.

LONDON - Britain's FTSE 100 index of blue-chip stocks ended a three-day winning streak as the prospect of an interest rate rise next week helped drag the market lower after initially scoring a record high.
Ending a budget week of extreme market volatility, the FTSE 100 closed at 4,812.8, down 18.9 points, or 0.39 percent. There was a rise of 172.5 from last week.

FRANKFURT - German shares kept up their record-setting pace, climbing nearly 1.5 percent due to strong overnight Wall Street gains and a German insurance industry merger that fuelled fresh demand for domestic shares.

The DAX-30 index closed at 3,942.53, up 55.14 points, or 1.42 percent, for a rise of of 147.12 on the week. In later screen-based trade the IBIS DAX index ended at 3,946.73, up 7.00 points, or 0.18 percent.
PARIS - French shares finished fractionally lower after a quiet session as U.S. financial markets were closed for the July 4 holiday.
The CAC-40 index closed at 2,934.48, down 2.50 points or 0.09 percent but up 43.44 points from last week.
ZURICH - Swiss shares held Thursday's winning streak, ending at another record close in the wake of continued investor interest in a few bourse heavyweights such as Roche, Novartis and Nestle.
The Swiss market index closed at 5,846.5, up 41.6 points or 0.72 percent and up 146.2 on the week.
MILAN - Italian shares closed mixed in a relatively subdued session with overseas investor interest curtailed by the U.S. independence day holiday.
The All Share Mibtel index closed at 13,608, up 5 points, or 0.04 percent, and up 220 points on the week.
AMSTERDAM - Dutch shares spent a low-volume day hovering range-bound in record territory, finishing more than one percent higher.
The AEX index closed at a record 907.19, up 10.09 points or 1.12 percent. There was a rise of 36.74 from last week.

TOKYO - The stock market's benchmark Nikkei index ended below the 20,000 level, the first time it has done so since the end of May, depressed by news that construction firm Tokai Kogyo had decided to apply for court protection, brokers said.
The 225-share Nikkei average closed at 19,968.00, down 153.41 points, or 0.76 percent. This was down 555.75 from last Friday.
HONG KONG - Stocks tumbled to a sharply lower close as uncertainty about government plans to curb rising real estate prices rattled property stocks.
The Hang Seng index closed at 14,822.97, down 232.77 points, or 1.55 percent for a fall of 373.82 points on the week.
SYDNEY - The stock market chalked up modest losses by the close as caution crept in ahead of the Independence Day holiday in U.S. markets.
The All Ordinaries index closed at 2,733.4, down 9.5 points, or 0.35 percent, but showed a rise of 31 points from the previous Friday's close.
JOHANNESBURG - Gold shares finished more than three percent weaker in quiet trade after bullion slid to 12-year lows, dealers said.

The All-share index closed at 7,368.0, down 35.2 points, or 0.48 percent, and down 43.2 from a week ago. The All Gold index closed at 952.1, down 33.1 points, or 0.32 percent, for a drop of 42.7 since last week. The Industrial index closed at 8,801.9, down 27.9 points, or 3.36 percent. This was up 54.3 from last Friday.
